messages:
Aisha (Finance): Hey @Linh and @Tom — got an invoice from VendorConcierge with a big "Data Processing" line that doesn't match our committed SKUs. See line: "Data Processing - 3,200 units - $9,600". Can someone confirm what "units" map to? I thought we were on a committed plan (50k tokens/month) not per-unit. /cc @ProcureBot

Tom (Platform): I saw that too. Our billing export shows a spike of ingestion events on 2026-03-12. Did they rename SKUs? Can you paste the invoice ID so I can cross-check?

Aisha (Finance): Invoice VC-2026-3213. The invoice references SKU `VC.DP.v2` — we don't have that in our internal SKU mapping doc.

Linh (Procurement): Thanks. I'm going to open a ticket with the AM. Proposed next steps: 1) ask VendorConcierge for the raw usage CSV for that invoice period, 2) request a SKU-to-feature mapping (what VC.DP.v2 actually measures), and 3) request a temporary credit while they investigate. Anyone have the API call to pull their usage export?

Tom (Platform): You can pull it via their billing API: ```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $VC_API' 'https://api.vendorconcierge.com/v1/billing/usage?start=2026-03-01&end=2026-03-31' > vc_usage.csv
``` Their CSV header looks like: `invoice_id,timestamp,sku,units,unit_price,region,customer_id`. Example row I saw: `VC-2026-3213,2026-03-12T14:03:21Z,VC.DP.v2,3200,3.00,us-west,redwood-prod`.

Aisha (Finance): I pulled vc_usage.csv and attached a short snippet: ```invoice_id,timestamp,sku,units,unit_price,region,customer_id
VC-2026-3213,2026-03-12T14:03:21Z,VC.DP.v2,3200,3.00,us-west,redwood-prod``` Looks like "units" might be documents processed from a new ingestion pipeline we launched.

ProcureBot: Support ticket created: VC-TSK-9987 with VendorConcierge. Priority: high. Assigned to: @VC_AM_Sarah. ETA for initial response: 24-48h. :white_check_mark:

Linh (Procurement): I'll ask the AM for: the definitive interpretation of VC.DP.v2, any announcement that was sent, and whether this is a new metered SKU or migration of an old one. If this is a pricing change without notice we should request pro-rated credit plus a one-month waiver while we reconcile.

Tom (Platform): FWIW, our deploy logs show we enabled a new "ingest" workflow on 2026-03-12 as part of release `2026.3.5`. That could have caused additional vendor calls. I'm running a query now to count vendor API calls by day and will paste the numbers shortly.

Aisha (Finance): Ok — thanks everyone. If VendorConcierge refuses to credit we'll escalate to procurement leadership. Please keep updates in this thread. :pray:
